verdict.rationale: Moss documents an in-process, on-device runtime through its Node, Python, Swift, Elixir, C and browser/WASM builds. It indexes and queries locally, embeds with a built-in model, and includes unlimited local queries. However, the local model is tied to the cloud: indexes hydrate from the cloud, sessions sync back to it, and the disk cache is a snapshot of cloud data, so a fully standalone embedded mode is not documented. Missing for 10: documented fully offline/standalone embedded operation without a cloud project, a lightweight local server/instance mode, explicit guidance for development and small workloads, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the database embedded in-process or as a lightweight local instance for development and small workloads

citations.quote: It runs in the browser, on-device, or in the cloud - wherever your agent lives - so search feels native.
index and query locally during a conversation, then sync to the cloud
One model across every surface: JavaScript (Node), Python, Swift (iOS), Elixir, C, and an in-browser/WASM build.
Moss embeds on-device with a built-in model
All plans include unlimited local queries.
The Node (`@moss-js/moss`) and Python SDKs can cache the downloaded index to disk so subsequent loads skip the download when the cloud data hasn’t changed.
a WebAssembly build that runs in the browser
